issues.title: [Bug]: list and mapping constant declarations are accepted where the corpus tests expect an error
issues.reasoning: Behaviour matches the issue (compiles and prints the values). Clean-context spec check: NOT-A-BUG. The spec's 'Constant expressions' section lists structural-constructor-expr and equality-expr as const-expr forms. 'Module constant declaration' only requires an anydata, non-never type that contains the expression's static type. So these declarations are legal, and the corpus tests subset8/08-list/6-e, 17-e and 08-mapping/6-e, 7-e are wrong and should be converted to -v tests.
issues.close_reason: Not a bug: list/mapping constructors and == of them are valid const-exprs per spec; convert the four corpus -e tests to -v instead.

issues.title: [Bug]: module initializer order ignores function global dependencies
issues.output:
error: interface conversion: values.BalValue is nil, not *values.Object
        at g(i1282a.bal:20)
           init(i1282a.bal:12)

(cycle variant)
1
issues.reasoning: Re-triaged after a new comment with variants. Previously undetermined because the spec doesn't define init order. The new variant changes that: initializing in source order lets the interpreter read an uninitialized module variable and crash with a Go interface-conversion error (or produce values not belonging to the declared type). Clean-context spec check: VALID-BUG for the dependency variant, since the spec doesn't constrain declaration order and a valid dependency order exists. The cycle variant (`int a = f(); f reads a` prints 1) is UNCLEAR per spec, which has no explicit cycle rule; a cycle error is the most defensible behaviour. Init ordering is computed in desugar (dependencyVisitor/toplogicallySortInits), so frontend. The crash happens at runtime, so not frontend-crash. Related: #1483, #1322, #1327.

undetermined.reasoning: Reproduces (each line compiles, then panics at runtime: arithmetic overflow / divide by zero / arithmetic overflow / bad type cast). Clean-context spec check: NOT required by spec. These are not const-expr contexts, and the arithmetic sections say int overflow and division by zero panic. But 'Singleton typing' says the static type is computed by compile-time evaluation and doesn't say what happens when that evaluation panics, so a compile error is also defensible. The decimal case depends on the implementation's exponent range. This needs a team/spec decision: if compile errors are wanted, label frontend (related #1262, #1130); otherwise close and fix the corpus -e tests.

Re-checked after a new comment, which adds four more nvim-harness nits (compiler-tools/ls-nvim-harness: Harness.request false handling, probe.sh quoting, empty replacement text, README prerequisite). Still a language-server/tooling tracker, not a language bug. None of langlib/triage-lib/frontend/backend fits. Suggest removing triage and applying the team's language-server/tooling label.
